title: The Cobra Effect: When Chasing Metrics Ruins Your Life
alt_title_1: Goodhart's Law: The Trap Behind Vanity Metrics
alt_title_2: How Colonial Delhi Accidentally Multiplied Its Cobras
description_hook: As the story goes, when colonial officials paid a bounty for dead cobras in Delhi, people started breeding cobras for the cash. This video shows how Goodhart's Law explains why chasing vanity metrics backfires.

scenes.headline: How a Snake Bounty Multiplied Snakes
scenes.stat_label: MORE WILD COBRAS AFTER DELHI'S BOUNTY BACKFIRED
bullets: Officials paid cash for every dead cobra skin delivered
Incentives quietly rewired human behavior overnight
scenes.narration: As the story goes, when colonial officials in Delhi offered cash for every dead cobra, the city ended up with even more venomous snakes.
scenes.source: The 'cobra effect' anecdote, named by economist Horst Siebert (2001); historical details are disputed

scenes.headline: From Backyard Snake Farms to Goodhart's Law
bullets: Enterprising locals bred cobras indoors for steady payouts
Canceled bounty -> worthless snakes released into Delhi
scenes.narration: Locals started breeding cobras in backyard sheds just to collect the payout. When officials discovered the scheme and canceled the bounty, breeders released the worthless snakes into the streets.
scenes.source: The 'cobra effect' anecdote, named by economist Horst Siebert (2001)

scenes.headline: When Measures Become Targets, They Break
scenes.left_body: Fake desk hours, app streaks, viral vanity views
scenes.right_body: Rare skills, finished products, net cashflow margin
scenes.narration: In 1975, British economist Charles Goodhart observed that a number used as a target stops measuring what it used to. Anthropologist Marilyn Strathern later put it simply: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
scenes.source: Charles Goodhart (1975); Marilyn Strathern, European Review (1997)

scenes.headline: Audit Your Personal Vanity Metrics
scenes.stat_subtext: Track metrics lightly • Optimize for real-world capability
scenes.narration: You fall into the same trap whenever you chase hours logged at a desk, app streaks, or vanity views instead of real skills and cashflow margin.

scenes.headline: Use Numbers as a Compass, Never an Idol
scenes.stat_label: SEPARATE THE PROXY FROM THE PRIZE
bullets: Ask: could I hit this number while getting worse?
Reward lasting output over cosmetic dashboards
scenes.narration: Use numbers as a quiet compass, never as your identity, because the second you worship the scoreboard you start gaming yourself.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
